title: Take one language-model SGD step
statement:
Step 11 · Train and generate

A bigram model learns a next-token distribution conditioned on one previous token. It isolates the language-model loss and optimizer before adding transformer backpropagation. For softmax cross entropy the logit gradient is p − one_hot(target).

Build it

Return a new logit table after one full-batch SGD step. Average gradients over all nonempty training pairs, including repeated previous-token rows. Compute all probabilities from the original table, then update once. rate is positive; IDs are valid.

Contract: Implement train_step using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: logits = [[0, 0], [0, 0]], pairs = [[0, 1], [1, 0]], rate = 0.2
Expected: [[-0.05, 0.05], [0.05, -0.05]]
Input: logits = [[1, 0], [0, 1]], pairs = [[0, 1], [0, 1]], rate = 0.1
Expected: [[0.9268941421369995, 0.07310585786300049], [0.0, 1.0]]
Hint

Accumulate a gradient table first. Updating after every pair would implement a different optimizer step.

Review your understanding

Why does this train only a bigram model? What extra derivatives and saved activations does transformer training require?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
